name: coverage
description:
Every distinct core phrase checked against the texts: a table phrase, count, docs, density and first.

mode: 'exact' — the words of the phrase in a row, case and ё folded; 'lemmas' — the same by lemmas of both sides; 'any_order' — the lemmas of the phrase all inside one piece of text (one phrase of split-text), in any order; a piece with them is one occurrence.
gap: how many words may stand between each two neighbouring words of the phrase in 'exact' and 'lemmas' («купить недорогие пластиковые окна» is «купить пластиковые окна» with gap 1); the order stays and a gap never crosses a sentence end; 0 allows none. It does not apply to 'any_order', where the words are already anywhere in one piece.
text_column: the column of the texts.

exact and lemmas cross any punctuation inside a sentence («хранения — это» is «хранения это», a comma too), never a sentence end (. ! ? …; the point of an abbreviation such as «г.» is none). The rows follow the core order; a phrase that is not found stays with count 0, as the missing phrases are the point. The columns:
- count: occurrences in all texts; one phrase does not overlap itself, and each phrase is counted on its own;
- docs: the texts that hold the phrase at least once;
- density: count x words of the phrase / words of all texts, a share from 0 to 1, rounded to 4 decimals;
- first: the number of the word (1-based, all words of the text counted) where the phrase first starts, in the first text that holds it; empty when count is 0.

against: a file with the texts, one per row; the file is read like `read` does. The texts are in --text-column, by default the first text column of the file.

The step takes the working column as the core; the table phrase, count, docs, density and first replaces the current one.

Example: semkit read core.csv coverage --against texts.csv write out.csv
